solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Showy trick with light not suitable for all ages

parts.note: a flam is an old word for a deception or trick

indicators.note: says the certificate letter is not kept in the word for light

parts.note: buoyant means light, able to float
U is the British film certificate for films anyone may watch

explanation.surface: A flashy stunt involving lighting that is unsuitable for children.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for 'universal', suitable for all ages; 'not' strips it from BUOYANT, leaving BOYANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something flamboyant is flashy and ostentatious, designed to be noticed.

clue.text: Full English — the lot!

parts.note: fat as in full, plump or well filled

explanation.surface: Ordering a full English breakfast, with everything on it.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'full English' is a British cooked breakfast; the surface asks for the whole plate, but 'the lot' is one's destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: one's lot in life is one's destiny, what fortune has allotted.

clue.text: Clothing engineers dressed in to shock

indicators.note: the engineers are clothed by, put inside, the word for shock

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers turning up in outrageous outfits to shock people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: apparel is a formal word for garments one wears.

clue.text: Defensive line-up makes one spectate, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a formation of players at the back, the defenders in a team
a word formed by trimming a supposed suffix, as the verb spectate was made from spectator

explanation.surface: A team's defensive setup makes a player stand and watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a term from linguistics: 'spectate' was coined by cutting back the older noun 'spectator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a sporting arrangement of rear players, and a linguistic term for a word derived by removing an apparent affix.

clue.text: PM coming up with ungrammatical statement of left-wing views created outcry

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the name is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: Theresa May was the British Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared
'me red' is a broken-English way of saying 'I am red', i.e. left-wing

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister rising amid a garbled leftist slogan caused uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns MAY into YAM; 'me red' is the pidgin form of 'I am a red'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to yammer is to complain loudly and persistently, a clamour of protest.

clue.text: Acknowledge refusal to put time into party

parts.note: no is a refusal

indicators.note: the time letter is placed into the party word

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Declining to spend time at a party, with a polite nod.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to nod to something is to recognise or give it a brief acknowledgement.

clue.text: Male politician's a plant

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
MP, Member of Parliament, is a British politician

explanation.surface: A male politician is a plant, a planted spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a politician who is a secret infiltrator; 'plant' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: cannabis sativa is the fibre-yielding crop grown for rope and cloth.

clue.text: Denial by goalkeeper accused of letting balls in? Flipping excuse

indicators.note: flipping turns the keeper's denial back to front

parts.words: Denial by goalkeeper accused of letting balls in
parts.note: a keeper accused of letting goals in would deny it: 'No, I save!'

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper denying letting goals in offers a lame excuse.
explanation.walkthrough: The keeper's protest 'NO I SAVE', read backwards under 'Flipping', gives the answer; 'flipping' also works as a mild British curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: an evasion is a dodge or pretext used to avoid the truth.

clue.text: Cut up United's back three and rush inside wearing City kit?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to snip is to cut

indicators.note: the rush word goes inside the three letters
the last three letters of the team name

parts.note: to rip is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: A football report of a City side cutting open United's defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City kit' is not a football strip: the City is London's financial district, where bankers wear striped suits. United's back three letters are TED.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: City of London bankers traditionally wear suits with thin vertical stripes.

clue.text: Subject to endless selection

indicators.note: the selection word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pick is a choice or selection

explanation.surface: Something exposed to selection without end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a subject is a theme or matter under discussion.

clue.text: Having hatched plot ringing round, I left no doubt

indicators.note: the phrase rings around, encloses, the I

parts.note: having hatched a plot is having made a plan

explanation.surface: A conspirator who hatched a plot made their intentions clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to make something plain is to make it clear beyond question.

clue.text: Aspire to act, failing with realisation in the end? That's about right

definitions.text: Aspire to act, failing with realisation in the end? That's about right

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the right letter
failing suggests the words break down and are reshuffled
take the final letter of realisation

explanation.surface: Meaning to act but never doing it until realising too late: that sums it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges ASPIRETOACT plus N, the end of 'realisation'; 'about' wraps that around R. The whole clue also describes the habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue is a description: delaying, aspiring to act but not doing so, is the habit of putting things off.

clue.text: Judge applying law to old record is court's ultimate arch manipulator?

parts.note: a ref, referee, judges a match
lex is Latin for law
a log is a written record

indicators.note: the last letter of court's

explanation.surface: A judge applying the law to an old record is the court's ultimate scheming mastermind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch manipulator' looks like a master schemer, but the arch is the foot's arch, worked by a foot-massage therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: a therapist who massages pressure points on the feet literally manipulates arches.

clue.text: Producer of wall-to-wall coverage getting grief over Trump's inauguration runs into ex-president

parts.note: pain is grief or distress

indicators.note: the beginning, the first letter, of Trump's
the runs letter is placed into the president's name

parts.note: George Bush, a former US president
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Wall-to-wall media coverage of grief at Trump's inauguration, with a former president involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wall-to-wall coverage' sounds like saturation news; it is literal paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a decorator's tool spreads paint across whole walls.

clue.text: It'll provoke a reaction from smaller gentlemen

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something that will draw a reaction from shorter men.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an allergy-triggering substance provokes an immune reaction.

clue.text: Tea approaching for audience in Sultan's place

indicators.note: the phrase is meant to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a brew, tea, that is nigh, approaching

explanation.surface: Tea about to be served for guests at the Sultan's palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brew' is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Fact: this small state on Borneo is ruled by a sultan.

clue.text: Spooner's Happy Meal's a riot

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: fun means happy, enjoyable
a bite is a light meal

explanation.surface: A children's fast-food meal causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy Meal' is a McDonald's children's meal; swapping the opening sounds of 'fun bite' gives the answer, a British term for a squabble or tea party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bun fight is a noisy squabble or tea party, a scrap of sorts.

clue.text: Divine drink breaking trance

indicators.note: the word trance is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavenly drink snapping someone out of a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Myth: the Greek gods drank this along with eating ambrosia.

clue.text: Practical old man splitting wire

indicators.note: the father word splits the wire word apart

parts.note: a cable is a wire
pa, father, is slang for one's old man

explanation.surface: A handy old fellow cutting through a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a practical person is competent and able.

clue.text: Note, in distress I can sue for offence

indicators.note: the words are distressed, put into disorder

explanation.surface: A distressed letter-writer threatening to sue over a slight.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: public or private nuisance is an offence or wrong in law.

clue.text: Knight heartlessly fuelled rioting with demands

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: rioting means the remaining letters run wild and are rearranged
the central letter of fuelled is removed

explanation.surface: A knight stirring up riots with his demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the central L of FUELLED, leaving FUELED, which 'rioting' reshuffles. The definition is the noun sense, as in 'doing the needful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: what is required or necessary, the necessities a situation calls for.

clue.text: Immersion heater's an ordeal

definitions.meaning: read cryptically, a dipping in water together with flames
a tough first experience or test

explanation.walkthrough: An immersion heater is a British electric water heater in a tank; here baptism is the immersion and fire the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a harsh initiation, originally a soldier's first experience of battle.

clue.text: Crop rotation affecting north of US state

indicators.note: the N, for north, is turned on its side, which makes it look like Z

parts.note: Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: Crop rotation in a northern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the letter N through ninety degrees and it becomes Z; 'crop rotation' is the farming practice the surface borrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: corn is a cereal grain grown as a major field crop.

clue.text: Slight lack of clarity in articulation

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an insulting remark, and speech so blurred that sounds run together.

clue.text: Determined Ben Gunn starts to dig incessantly all over the place

indicators.note: the letters are scattered and rearranged
the first letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: The castaway Ben Gunn digging relentlessly everywhere for treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben Gunn is the marooned man in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: unbending means resolute, refusing to yield.

clue.text: Terrible guillotine permitted

indicators.note: the guillotine cuts off the head, the first letter

parts.note: lawful means permitted by law

explanation.surface: Executing by guillotine is permitted, which is terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: awful means dreadful, very bad.

clue.text: Ran and took shelter, conserving energy

indicators.note: the shelter word keeps the energy letter inside it

parts.note: hid means took cover
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone ran and hid, saving their strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: to hie is to hasten or go quickly.

clue.text: Hit top note, returning after time without piano

parts.note: to best is to top or beat

indicators.note: the reversed note comes after the time word
the piano letter is taken out

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: the note is read backwards

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer hits a top note, coming back after a while without the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit top note' reads as singing, but 'Hit' is the definition and 'top' the first piece; 'without' drops P from SPELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hit is a big commercial success, such as a book selling very well.
